We study the interplay between attention and recurrence in sequence transduction, and we show that a purely attentional architecture suffices for strong results on two machine translation benchmarks.

The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder, and the best performing models connect the two through an attention mechanism.

Attention computes the alignment aij between every pair of positions, and the whole model is fully parallelizable.
